body:

write-ups, postmortems, or a public roadmap log). Premature with zero entries.

title: Create a Catena Dashboard demo
body:
- Build it as a static webpage replicating a Catena Admin deployment, with no interactive fields.
- Optionally base it on screenshots from a real deployment, with credentials hidden. Add a few apps and their settings.
- Make its primary zone "catena.run".
- Make it a Business licensed instance.
- Deploy a new version of the page on each Catena release.
- Deploy it on GitHub Pages at demo.catena.run.
- Add a link in the top menu bar of catena.run.

Moved from catenahq/ops#391.

title: Fix the editions section for backups
body:
Automatic backups are available to every edition. Frequency is limited to weekly for Community, and is unlimited for Pro
and Business.

- **Behaviour:** the edition comparison's "Data and backups" group shows one row in place of `weekly_backups` and
  `scheduled_backups` (`src/i18n/en/common.json` and `src/i18n/fr/common.json`, `pricing_matrix.groups.data.rows`):

  | Automatic backups | Weekly | Unlimited | Unlimited |

  FR: "Sauvegardes automatiques | Hebdomadaire | Illimitée | Illimitée". Text in place of check marks or crosses is
  fine. No cadence figure on the website.
- **Acceptance:** the website build passes, EN and FR in parity; the capability cells still match the feature manifest
  (ops `automation/operator-tools/generate-pricing-matrix.py --check`): if the merged row needs a features.yml owner,
  propose the features.yml change in the commit manifest.

Moved from catenahq/ops#494.

title: The terms page contradicts the agreements and links none of them
body:
The terms page (`src/i18n/*/common.json` `terms`) calls the engagement letter the canonical contract and sets the SLA and termination terms "in your engagement letter", where the agreements (contracts `legal/master-agreement.md`) record the Edition on an Order Form. It describes the billing as a flat retainer and the SLA as reviewed at the quarterly check-in. The master agreement's section 3.1 already says no minimum term, so the terms page and the agreement agree on that. No page links to `/{en,fr}/legal/*`; the pages are served by `src/pages/[locale]/legal/[doc].astro`.

- **Behaviour:** the terms page reconciles its engagement-letter wording with the agreements' Order Form, and its retainer and quarterly check-in wording with the agreements, and links each agreement through `src/pages/[locale]/legal/[doc].astro`, in English and French.
- **Security notes:** none.
- **Acceptance:** the website build passes; the terms page links each agreement.

The agreements were rewritten to the three editions in contracts d1c2bd0 (catenahq/contracts#23, closed).

title: M15. Website: visual schema of how the suite fits together
body:
The capability list on the homepage (and the per-capability sections
on `/features/`) communicate WHAT we deliver but not HOW the pieces
interoperate. Prospects who learn visually need a flowchart / schema
diagram showing chat -> meetings -> phone -> CRM -> files -> etc.,
with the integration arrows that make Catena one stack instead of a
bag of apps.

Required IN ADDITION TO the existing list, not instead of it. The
list answers "do you cover X?"; the schema answers "how do my tools
talk to each other?"

How to apply: design pass + marketing review before the rework lands
on `website/`. Render as an SVG so the diagram scales with the
viewport and stays sharp on both light + dark themes. Bilingual
labels per the EN/FR parity rule.

Filed in ops internal_docs/sales/BACKLOG.md on 2026-11-12.

<!-- backlog-id: b8fcccb0918b16d047aed2575f5e48cd5827a1c8 -->

Moved from catenahq/ops#428.

title: "Secure connections" feature card is too wordy
body:
The goal of the card is to broadly show features, not describe their spec.

"Keeps your services safe through dedicated Admin and App tunnels, with DDoS protection. Keeps your server safe with automatic firewall and port reconciliation."

Also fix the French version to match
